examples.ko: 샤워기 배수구가 막혀서 물이 안 내려가요.
examples.en: The shower drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.
There is a lot of hair stuck in the drain.
A smell came up from the drain, so I cleaned it.
I bought a product to unclog the sink drain.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길가 배수구로 물이 넘쳤어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so water overflowed from the drain by the road.

examples.ko: 배수구 덮개는 자주 씻어 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You need to wash the drain cover often.

explain: 욕실이나 싱크대, 길가에서 물이 빠져나가는 구멍이에요. '하수구'도 비슷하게 쓰는데, 하수구는 더러운 물이 흘러가는 길이나 관까지 넓게 가리켜요.

phrases.en: The sink drain is clogged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 안 내려갈 때 가장 먼저 떠오르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The first phrase that comes to mind when water won't go down.

phrases.en: I unclogged the blocked drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막힌 곳을 시원하게 통하게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you clear a blockage so water flows again.

phrases.en: I clean the bathroom drain every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리카락이나 때를 치우는 일상적인 청소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to everyday cleaning of hair and dirt from the drain.

explain_en: The opening where water drains, in streets, bathrooms, buildings. It is the opening where water drains away in a bathroom, sink or roadside. '하수구' is used similarly, but it can also refer more broadly to the channel or pipe that carries dirty water.

t90.ax: You need to wash the drain cover often.

examples.en: New security lights were installed in every alley.
Thanks to the security lights, walking at night is less scary.

examples.ko: 주민들이 보안등을 더 달아 달라고 요청했어요.
examples.en: Residents asked for more security lights to be put up.
Children are playing under the glow of the security light.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 보안등은 해가 지면 저절로 켜져요.
examples.en: The security lights in our neighborhood turn on by themselves at sunset.

examples.ko: 고장 난 보안등에 안내문이 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: A notice is stuck on the broken security light.

explain: 골목이나 주택가의 밤길을 안전하게 하려고 세운 등이에요. 큰길의 '가로등'과 비슷하지만 방범 목적이 더 강해요. 동네 민원이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: When the sun set, the security lights came on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어두워질 때 등이 저절로 켜지는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes lights coming on as it gets dark.

phrases.example: 어두운 골목에 보안등을 달아 달라고 신청했어요.
phrases.en: I applied to have a security light installed in the dark alley.
phrases.nuance_ko: 등을 설치한다는 뜻으로, 동네 일을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means installing a light; common in talk about neighborhood matters.

phrases.en: The streetlights are shining brightly on the main road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보안등'과 비슷하지만 '가로등'은 길을 비추는 큰길의 등을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 보안등, but 가로등 means the lights along main roads.

explain_en: These are lights set up in alleys and residential areas to make night streets safer. They are similar to '가로등' (street lamps) on main roads but have a stronger crime-prevention purpose. They come up in neighborhood complaints and news.

t90.ax: A notice is stuck on the broken security light.

examples.ko: 밤에 쥐가 부스럭거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: A mouse was rustling at night, so I couldn't sleep.
The person next to me keeps rustling a plastic bag.

examples.ko: 영화 중에 과자를 부스럭거리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't rustle snack bags during a movie.
I hear someone rustling around in the room.
The child rustled around under the blanket and then got up.
When I walk on fallen leaves, they rustle under my feet.

explain: 마른 종이, 비닐, 낙엽처럼 마른 것이 스치는 소리가 나거나 그런 소리를 내며 움직인다는 말이에요. '부스럭대다'도 같은 뜻이에요. '바스락거리다'는 조금 더 가볍고 작은 소리 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling rustled around at dawn and woke me up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부스럭거리다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 조금 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 부스럭거리다, a bit more casual.

phrases.en: I hear a rustling sound in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 설명할 때 '-는'을 붙여서 명사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use the -는 form before 소리 to describe the sound.

phrases.en: Fallen leaves rustle when you step on them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부스럭거리다'보다 가볍고 작은 소리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lighter, smaller sound than 부스럭거리다.

explain_en: Heavier rustle of moving things, standard form (부스럭거리다) It describes the dry sound of things like paper, plastic or leaves rubbing together, or moving while making that sound. '부스럭대다' means the same thing. '바스락거리다' feels a little lighter and softer in sound.

t90.ax: I hear someone rustling around in the room.

examples.en: They piled rice high on my plate.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 온 집의 창가에 먼지가 수북이 쌓였어요.
examples.en: Dust had piled up on the windowsill since I hadn't been home in a while.
Fallen leaves lay piled in heaps across the yard.

examples.ko: 배가 고파서 밥을 수북이 퍼서 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was hungry, so I scooped a heaping portion of rice and ate it.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 서류가 수북이 쌓인 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw documents piled high on the desk.

examples.ko: 눈이 수북이 쌓여서 차가 못 다녀요.
examples.en: Snow has piled up deep, so cars can't get through.

explain: '수북하다'의 부사형이에요. '가득'은 그릇이 꽉 찬 것이고, '수북이'는 그릇 위로 솟아오를 만큼 쌓인 모양이에요.

phrases.en: The plate is heaped with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '수북이'의 기본이 되는 형용사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective that 수북이 comes from.

phrases.en: I heaped fruit in the bowl.
phrases.nuance_ko: '담다'와 함께 쓰면 그릇 위로 솟게 가득 담는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 담다, it means filling above the rim.

phrases.en: The snow piled up deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 되풀이해서 쌓인 모습을 더 생생하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The repeated form makes the piling more vivid.

explain_en: It is the adverb form of '수북하다'. '가득' means filled to the brim, while '수북이' means piled up so high it rises above the rim.

t90.ax: They piled rice high on my plate.

examples.en: I put rice and seasoned vegetables in a big bowl and mixed them.

examples.ko: 엄마가 양푼에 떡볶이를 가득 담아 주셨어요.
examples.en: Mom filled a big bowl with tteokbokki for us.

examples.ko: 양푼 비빔밥은 숟가락으로 막 비벼 먹어야 맛있어요.
examples.en: Bibimbap in a big bowl tastes best when you mix it roughly with a spoon.
Where did our big bowl go?

examples.ko: 양푼 하나에 다섯 명이 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: Five of us ate together from one big bowl.
You can use a big bowl for a long time even if it gets dented.

explain: 음식을 담거나 비빌 때 쓰는 큰 그릇이에요. '양푼 비빔밥'처럼 여럿이 함께 먹는 편한 분위기와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I shared a big bowl of bibimbap with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 그릇에 비벼서 여럿이 같이 먹는 편한 분위기의 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual dish mixed in a big bowl and shared with many people.

phrases.en: I filled the big bowl with kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 그릇에 음식을 많이 담는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means putting a lot of food into a large bowl.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in a big bowl

phrases.en: I brought a big bowl full of fruit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇이 크고 음식이 넉넉하다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of a large bowl with plenty of food.

explain_en: It is a big bowl used for holding or mixing food. It fits the relaxed mood of eating together, as in '양푼 비빔밥'.

examples.ko: 그는 밧줄 한쪽 끝을 묶어 올가미를 만들었어요.
examples.en: He tied one end of the rope and made a loop snare.
Be careful not to get your foot caught in the snare.
The rabbit was caught in a snare and couldn't move.

examples.ko: 그 계약은 사실 사기꾼이 파 놓은 올가미였어요.
examples.en: That contract was actually a trap set by a swindler.
I want to get away from rules that feel like a trap.

examples.ko: 올가미를 던져 말을 잡는 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a video of someone throwing a lasso to catch a horse.

explain: 줄 끝을 고리로 만들어 동물이나 물건을 잡는 도구예요. 비유로 '빠져나오기 힘든 함정'이라는 뜻으로도 써요. '덫'은 여러 가지 장치를 모두 가리켜서 조금 더 넓어요.

phrases.en: A rabbit got caught in the snare.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이나 사람이 걸려 잡힌 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes being caught in a snare.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a snare

phrases.en: The cowboy threw a lasso toward the horse.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄 고리를 던져 잡는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes throwing a loop of rope to catch something.

phrases.en: The hunter set a trap in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '올가미'보다 넓게 여러 가지 장치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Broader than 올가미, covering all kinds of traps.

explain_en: It is a tool made by forming a loop at the end of a rope to catch an animal or object. Figuratively it also means a trap that is hard to escape. '덫' is a little broader, covering all kinds of trapping devices.

examples.en: The plate fell and smashed with a crash.
The window shattered with a loud crash.
The shelf collapsed with a crash and I was startled.
A cat passing by knocked a cup down with a crash.
I heard a crash and ran to the kitchen.

examples.ko: 화분이 와장창 넘어지는 소리에 잠이 깼어요.
examples.en: I woke up at the sound of a flowerpot crashing over.

explain: 물건이 한꺼번에 깨지거나 무너질 때 나는 요란한 소리예요. '쨍그랑'은 유리나 그릇이 깨지는 소리에 주로 쓰고, '와장창'은 더 크고 여러 개가 무너지는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The glass bottle shattered with a crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어와 '깨지다'를 함께 쓴 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 깨지다.

phrases.en: The stacked boxes collapsed with a crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개가 한꺼번에 무너지는 큰 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the loud sound of many things collapsing at once.

phrases.example: 컵이 바닥에 떨어져서 쨍그랑 소리가 났어요.
phrases.en: The cup fell on the floor and made a clanging crash.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 소리말로, 유리나 그릇 하나가 깨지는 소리에 주로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar sound word, mainly for a single glass or dish breaking.

explain_en: It is the loud sound of things breaking or collapsing all at once. '쨍그랑' is mainly the sound of glass or dishes breaking, while '와장창' feels bigger and more like many things falling apart.

examples.en: They repainted the exterior wall of the building.
The outer wall is cracked, so rain leaks in.

examples.ko: 아파트 외벽 공사 때문에 소리가 커요.
examples.en: It's loud because of the exterior wall work at the apartment.
Ivy is growing on the outside wall.
In winter, a house with thick outer walls is warm.
Workers hang from ropes to clean the exterior wall.

explain: 건물의 바깥쪽을 둘러싼 벽이에요. 반대말은 안쪽의 '내벽'이에요. 공사나 건축 이야기에 자주 나오고, 평소에는 그냥 '벽'이라고 해도 돼요.

phrases.en: Next year they will do exterior wall work on the apartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물 겉벽을 고치거나 칠하는 일을 말해요. 건축 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Work to repair or paint a building's outer wall, common in construction talk.

phrases.en: We painted the outer wall white.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이나 페인트를 바꿀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for changing the color or paint of a building.

phrases.en: The outer wall cracked because of the earthquake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽이 갈라진 상태를 말할 때 써요. '갈라지다'보다 얇은 틈 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a cracked wall, with a feel of a thin crack rather than a big split.

explain_en: It is the wall on the outside of a building, and its opposite is 내벽, the inner wall. It appears in construction talk, though in casual speech people often just say 벽.

examples.ko: 책상 서랍이 잡동사니로 가득 차 있어요.
examples.en: The desk drawer is full of odds and ends.

examples.ko: 창고에서 잡동사니를 정리하다가 옛 사진을 찾았어요.
examples.en: While sorting junk in the storeroom, I found old photos.
Before moving, I'd better throw away the clutter first.
This box has nothing but odds and ends in it.
There is so much clutter that the room looks small.

examples.ko: 가방 속 잡동사니 때문에 열쇠를 못 찾겠어요.
examples.en: I can't find my keys because of all the stuff in my bag.

explain: 쓸모가 있는지 없는지 애매한 자잘한 물건들이 뒤섞여 있는 것을 말해요. 완전한 쓰레기와 달리 아직 버리지 않고 모아 둔 물건이라는 느낌이 있어요. '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Odds and ends are piled up on the balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자잘한 물건이 치우지 않은 채 많아졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means small items have piled up without being tidied.

phrases.en: I cleared out all the clutter before moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정리하다'보다 눈앞에서 없앤다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like removing things from sight than '정리하다'.

phrases.en: I found batteries in the junk box.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 가지 작은 물건을 아무렇게나 넣어 둔 상자를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a box where various small items are tossed in.

explain_en: It refers to small items of unclear use that are jumbled together. Unlike pure trash, it has a feel of things you have kept and not yet thrown away. It is often used as '잡동사니를 정리하다/버리다'.

en: to light; to turn on; to ignite

examples.en: When the athlete lit the torch, applause poured in.
Be careful when you light the burner.

examples.ko: 로켓 엔진을 점화한 지 몇 초 만에 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: The rocket lifted off just seconds after the engine was ignited.
I tried to light the candle with a lighter.
Check safety first, and then light it.
A loud noise came the moment it was ignited.

explain: 성화, 엔진, 버너처럼 불을 붙여 작동시키는 것이 목적어로 와요. 일상에서는 '불을 붙이다'나 '불을 켜다'라고 말하고, '점화하다'는 설명서나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I lit the gas stove.
phrases.nuance_ko: '점화하다'보다 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural in daily conversation than '점화하다'.

phrases.en: When the engine ignited, the rocket went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 붙어 작동하기 시작한다는 뜻으로, 주어가 불이 붙는 쪽이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form: the thing itself catches fire and starts working.

phrases.en: Put the water on after lighting the burner.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 뒤에'를 붙여 순서를 말하는 연결형이에요. 설명서에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for giving steps, often seen in instructions.

explain_en: Formal/written, ignite a device or flame (점화 장치, 초) Its objects are things lit to start working, such as torches, engines and burners. In daily life people say '불을 붙이다' or '불을 켜다', and '점화하다' appears more in manuals and news.

examples.en: The whole town lost power because of the storm.
The power suddenly went out and I could not see anything.
If the building loses power, the elevators stop.
While the power was out, we lit candles and talked.
I bought a flashlight in case the power goes out at night.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 정전되었는데 한 시간 뒤에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: The power went out last night and came back an hour later.

explain: 전기가 갑자기 끊길 때 써요. 일상에서는 '정전이 되다', '불이 나가다'라고 더 많이 말해요. 전기가 다시 들어오면 '전기가 들어오다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: There was a power outage in our neighborhood last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정전되다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '정전되다' and common in spoken Korean.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken expression.

phrases.en: The electricity came back on an hour later.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정전이 끝났을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the outage is over.

explain_en: Use it when electricity is suddenly cut. In daily speech people more often say '정전이 되다' or '불이 나가다'. When power returns, you say '전기가 들어오다'.

examples.ko: 비 때문에 창문에 판자를 대 놓았어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, I boarded up the window.
The man cut a plank and made a bookshelf.

examples.ko: 산비탈에 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 아직 몇 채 남아 있어요.
examples.en: A few houses built of old boards still remain on the hillside.

examples.ko: 판자가 썩어서 이 다리는 건너기 위험해요.
examples.en: The boards are rotten, so this bridge is dangerous to cross.
This board is thick and hard, so it is sturdy.

examples.ko: 마당 한쪽에 남은 판자를 쌓아 두었어요.
examples.en: I stacked the leftover planks in one corner of the yard.

explain: 얇고 넓게 자른 나무가 '판자'이고, 두껍고 긴 나무는 '각목'이라고 해서 모양으로 이름이 갈려요. '판자촌'은 낡은 판자로 지은 집이 모인 동네를 가리키는 말로 옛날 이야기에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I put a board over the hole in the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가를 막거나 덮으려고 판자를 붙일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when attaching a board to cover or block something.

phrases.en: Wooden planks are piled up in the storage room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료가 나무라는 것을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that the material is wood.

phrases.en: The children made a small house out of boards.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료가 판자라고 말할 때 '-(으)로'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -(으)로 to say the material is board.

explain_en: A '판자' is a thin, wide cut of wood, while a thick, long piece is called a '각목'. The word '판자촌' (shanty town) comes up often in stories about the past.

t90.ax: The man cut a plank and made a bookshelf.

examples.en: The drain is clogged, so the water won't go down.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 하수구에서 물이 넘쳐요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, water overflows from the drain.
Hair often gets stuck in the drain.
A sewer smell came up, so I opened the window.
I dropped my key down the drain.
Drains need to be cleaned regularly.

explain: 원래 길 아래 큰 물길은 '하수구', 집 안 욕실이나 싱크대의 구멍은 '배수구'라고 구별해요. 하지만 일상에서는 집 안의 구멍도 '하수구'라고 하는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.en: There's a sewer smell in the bathroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 길에서 나는 나쁜 냄새를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for bad smells in the home or street.

phrases.en: I cleaned the sink drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 안의 물 빠지는 구멍은 '배수구'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The drain hole inside a house is also called 배수구.

phrases.en: You must not pour oil down the drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경이나 생활 규칙을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about environment or household rules.

explain_en: The outlet or pipe that carries dirty water away (하수구가 막히다) Strictly, the large channel under the street is 하수구 and the hole in a bathroom or sink is 배수구. In daily life, though, many people call the one at home 하수구 as well.

t90.ax: I dropped my key down the drain.

examples.en: I turned on the kitchen fan and grilled fish.

examples.ko: 화장실 환풍기가 고장 나서 소리가 커요.
examples.en: The bathroom fan is broken, so it makes a lot of noise.
After I left the fan on, the smell went away.
Dust had built up on the fan, so I cleaned it.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 환풍기가 잘 돌아가서 냄새가 안 나요.
examples.en: This restaurant's fans run well, so there is no smell.

examples.ko: 환풍기 소리가 시끄러워서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: The fan is so loud that I can't sleep.

explain: 공기를 바꾸는 일은 '환기'이고, 그 일을 하는 기계가 '환풍기'예요. 부엌의 큰 환풍기는 '후드'라고도 많이 불러요. '환풍기를 켜다/끄다/틀다', '환풍기가 돌아가다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I turn off the exhaust fan when I finish cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of turning it on (켜다).

phrases.en: The fan keeps running, so it is noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환풍기가 작동하고 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the fan running.

phrases.en: I turned on the range hood and grilled meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부엌 환풍기를 일상에서 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word for the kitchen exhaust fan.

explain_en: Swapping the air in a room is '환기', and the machine that does it is a '환풍기'. The large fan above a stove is also commonly called a '후드'. You say '환풍기를 켜다/끄다/틀다' and '환풍기가 돌아가다'.
